messages:
alexa: Heads up — putting together a proposal for enforcing per-tenant isolation in our telemetry pipeline. main idea: route by resource.attributes.tenant_id in the OTEL collector, send to per-tenant exporters (GCS/BQ prefixes) + apply tenant-specific retention. looking for concerns and gaps before I write the RFC.

raj: routing in the collector makes sense for low-latency enforcement, but it increases cardinality on the collector and exporter set. do we plan one exporter per tenant or a prefix-based exporter?

alexa: good point. thinking prefix-based exporters (e.g., gcs://redwood-telemetry/tenant-{id}/) so we don't spawn N exporters. routing processor would map tenant_id -> exporter with dynamic config.

morgan: we should also think about sampling & PII scrubbing before routing. spans sometimes contain user emails in attributes. we need a processor that removes/obfuscates sensitive attributes per-tenant policy.

sam: security note — any per-tenant export must be backed by RBAC in the storage layer. even with prefixes, we must ensure KMS keys are scoped or encrypted per-tenant for high-priv customers. also audit logs.

kevin: from Console POV, per-tenant datasets map cleanly to per-tenant dashboards and RBAC. want to make sure the mapping is deterministic for customer-facing UI. can we guarantee tenant_id is always present and authoritative?

alexa: authoritative source will be request-routing layer (API + edge) that injects telemetry.resource.attributes.tenant_id. fallback if missing: tag as "unattributed" and route to shared dataset with alert for ops. we shouldn't silently drop.

otel-bot: note: there's an open PR with a prototype collector config: https://git.internal/r/redwood/otel-collector/pulls/82

raj: quick performance thought — prefix-based exporters plus a routing processor that has a regexp map should scale. avoid per-tenant exporters in the same process. maybe run a sidecar worker to flush to cloud storage to push down load.

morgan: also need to decide retention tiers: default 90d for hosted, enterprise can request 1y/7y. longer retention will blow up storage — need cost attribution and per-tenant quotas.

sam: compliance customers will want WORM/immutable retention for certain datasets. that implies a different exporter backend or storage policy. include that in the design.

alexa: sketching a minimal config (for discussion):

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc: {}
      http: {}
processors:
  attributes:
    actions:
      - key: tenant_id
        from_attribute: resource.attributes.tenant_id
  resource_to_telemetry
  routing:
    table:
      - value: "tenant-A"
        exporters: [tenant-a-prefix]
      - value: "tenant-B"
        exporters: [tenant-b-prefix]
      - default_exporters: [shared-prefix]
exporters:
  tenant-a-prefix:
    type: gcs
    bucket: redwood-telemetry
    object_prefix: "tenant-A/"
  shared-prefix:
    type: gcs
    bucket: redwood-telemetry
    object_prefix: "shared/"
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [attributes, routing]
      exporters: [tenant-a-prefix, tenant-b-prefix, shared-prefix]
```

kevin: that looks reasonable as a starter. question: how will console map exported files back to queryable indices/dashboards? do we run an ingest job that consumes per-tenant prefixes into our analytics cluster?

alexa: yes — downstream ingest job will read prefixes and write into per-tenant indices in ClickHouse/BigQuery. ingest layer enforces additional RBAC and can trigger alerts if data land in wrong place.

morgan: test plan idea: POC with 3 tenants, enable attribute-scrubbing processor, verify no PII in spans, verify retention TTLs enforced and cost accounting per-tenant. also chaos test where tenant_id is missing.

sam: add threat model: malicious tenant could try to craft tenant_id to route to other tenant prefix. routing must validate tenant_id against canonical tenant registry service (callout to account-service).

alexa: +1 on validation. plan for next steps: i) write RFC with config options (prefix vs per-exporter) ii) POC using the PR linked by otel-bot iii) add account-service validation and attribute-scrub processor iv) retention controls and billing hooks.

kevin: can we include an ops rollout playbook? e.g., start with non-prod tenants, monitor export counts, enable on-hosted customers with small footprints, then enterprise opt-ins.

raj: I'll schedule a 30m sync to go over collector resource implications and an infra-cost estimate.

morgan: if nobody objects, I'll own the POC and start with scrubbing + routing + ingest.

alexa: thanks — please add short notes to the PR and I'll draft the RFC. tagging security for review. :thumbsup:
